notes:
Net map (3 nets, no GND symbol anywhere in this drawing, so no net is named "0" - net names here are arbitrary labels, cf. the guide "names are arbitrary except ground"): n1 = the top rail between the two elements, i.e. right end of resistor 0 (2K), left end of inductor 3 (0.1H) and the top plate of capacitor 1, which hangs down from that rail at x=275. n2 = left rail: left end of resistor 0 -> top-left corner (161,183) -> down x~161 -> bottom-left corner (160,311) -> right along the bottom to the "-" (left) terminal of source 2. n3 = right rail + the mid horizontal: right end of inductor 3 -> top-right corner (372,183) -> down x~372 -> bottom-right corner (372,312) -> left along the bottom to the "+" (right) terminal of source 2; the mid horizontal at y=264-267 T-terminates on that right rail at (372,267) and carries the bottom plate of capacitor 1 (lead down x=274 to y=265).
COMPONENT RE-CLASS: component 2 was bootstrapped as "I-DC"; the symbol is a circle containing "-" and "+" with the label "50V" underneath (verified at 8x) - unmistakably a DC voltage source, not a current source (no arrow). Re-classed to V-DC. Terminal count is 2 either way, so nothing else changed; index 0 = left ("-") lead, index 1 = right ("+") lead.
Judgment calls: (a) THE KEY CALL - the mid horizontal (y=264) crosses the left rail (x=161-163) and overshoots ~6 px past it to x=155. There is no junction dot (both strokes are 2 px and the blob is 2 px; at y=263 there is even a 3 px gap between the overshoot stub and the rail, they only touch on row 264). I read it as a plain crossing, NOT a junction, because the junction reading puts the mid horizontal in parallel with the bottom rail and therefore short-circuits source 2 across its own terminals (the bootstrap did exactly that - it had both source terminals on one net) which is electrically absurd. With the crossing reading the drawing is the standard textbook circuit: 50 V source -> 2 K resistor -> 0.1 H inductor in parallel with 2 mF capacitor -> back to the source. A human should re-check this one crossing; the 6 px overshoot is the only thing that argues the other way. (b) The mid horizontal's right end genuinely terminates on the right rail (verified at 6x and pixel level - no ink to the right of x=372), so that end IS a junction. (c) The four long faint lines that run off the image edges (top right, far left, far right, bottom left) are ruled/edge lines on the paper, not circuit wires - they touch no component. (d) Two-terminal parts are indexed left->right except capacitor 1, which is drawn vertically and is indexed top plate then bottom plate.
